extra.message: User-controlled req.body.login is concatenated directly into the SQL string "SELECT name,id FROM Users WHERE login='" + req.body.login + "'" and passed to db.sequelize.query(). This allows SQL injection (e.g. ' OR '1'='1' UNION SELECT password,1 FROM Users --).

req.body.address is concatenated into a shell command passed to child_process.exec('ping -c 2 ' + req.body.address). An attacker can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. "127.0.0.1; id") to execute arbitrary OS commands.

Uploaded file contents are passed to node-serialize's serialize.unserialize(), which evaluates serialized functions (e.g. {"rce":"_$$ND_FUNC$$_function(){...}()"}). This leads to unauthenticated-remote-code-execution-class deserialization RCE on the legacy bulk import endpoint.

Uploaded XML is parsed with libxmljs.parseXmlString(..., {noent:true}), which expands external entities. A crafted DOCTYPE/ENTITY declaration can read local files (e.g. file:///etc/passwd) or perform SSRF, disclosing file contents in the product description.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: User input req.body.eqn is passed directly to mathjs.eval(). With the pinned mathjs 3.10.1 this allows sandbox escape via constructor access (cos.constructor("...")()) leading to arbitrary code/OS command execution.

cwe: CWE-95: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code ('Eval Injection')

extra.message: res.redirect(req.query.url) redirects to an unvalidated user-supplied URL. An attacker can craft /app/redirect?url=http://evil.example to send victims to a phishing site.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: The product search term is echoed with EJS's unescaped output tag <%- output.searchTerm %>. Since searchTerm comes from req.body.name, an attacker can inject script markup that executes in the victim's browser (reflected XSS).

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: Product id, name, code, tags and description are rendered with unescaped EJS tags <%- ... %>. Because product fields are attacker-controlled (add/modify product and bulk import), stored script payloads execute for any user viewing the product list (stored XSS).

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: User id, name and email fetched from /app/admin/usersapi are written into the DOM via innerHTML (c_name.innerHTML = users[i].name). A user can register with a name such as , causing DOM-based stored XSS for anyone visiting /app/admin/users.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The /app/admin/usersapi route only applies authHandler.isAuthenticated and never verifies req.user.role == 'admin'. Any authenticated non-admin can call the endpoint and retrieve all users, including password hashes. The admin check exists only client-side in admin.ejs.

userEditSubmit looks up and updates the user using the attacker-controlled hidden field req.body.id instead of req.user.id. By tampering with the id, any authenticated user can change another user's name, email and password (IDOR / broken object-level authorization).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: db.User.findAll({}) returns every User attribute, and listUsersAPI serializes the full objects to JSON (res.json({users: users})). This exposes bcrypt password hashes and other sensitive fields to any authenticated caller.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: The express-session secret is hardcoded to the well-known value 'keyboard cat'. Anyone who knows this can forge/decrypt session cookies and potentially bypass authentication.
The session cookie is configured with secure:false (and no httpOnly), so the session cookie is transmitted over plaintext HTTP and is accessible to client-side scripts, enabling session hijacking.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: The password reset token is simply md5(req.query.login), a predictable value derived from the publicly known username. An attacker can visit /resetpw?login=victim&token=md5(victim) and reset any user's password, bypassing authentication.

cwe: CWE-640: Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password

extra.message: State-changing POST routes such as /app/modifyproduct (and /app/useredit) are protected only by authentication, with no anti-CSRF token. The csurf dependency is present but never applied in server.js, so an attacker page can silently submit product edits or user profile/password changes on behalf of a logged-in victim.

The Sequelize connection is created without logging:false, so every SQL query (including inserts/selects containing password hashes) is written to the application log/console, exposing sensitive data to log readers.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: On a save error the raw Sequelize error object is flashed and later rendered to the user (req.flash('danger', err)). Combined with the calculator endpoint passing uncaught mathjs errors to Express's default handler, internal error details/stack traces are disclosed.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: Express is initialized without app.disable('x-powered-by'), so every response leaks the X-Powered-By: Express header, aiding framework fingerprinting.
